subject: Discovery: private/on‑prem requirements — CardioRisk Health
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Lana Ortiz <lana.ortiz@cardioriskhealth.com>, Samuel King <sam.king@cardioriskhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery: private/on‑prem requirements — CardioRisk Health

Hi Lana / Sam —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have aligned next steps. I tried to keep this concise; bolded items are blockers for any hosted option.

High-level pain / goals
- Process PHI-sensitive cardiac images and de-identified notes for model-driven triage.
- Zero tolerance for uncontrolled egress or vendor-managed key material.
- Want predictable latency and an option to run fully air-gapped for audit windows.

Current stack / constraints you shared
- On-prem Kubernetes (RHEL nodes), FHIR store behind an internal load balancer.
- Strict outbound firewall rules — only whitelisted IPs, no internet access from compute nodes except through proxy.
- Existing KMS/HSM (Thales) for all encryption; procurement requires customer-managed keys.
- SOC2 Type II + HIPAA obligations; internal Infosec reviews for any third-party agent.

Redwood Private fit & initial requirements (call takeaways)
- VPC-only deployment (no public endpoints) with optional private control plane in your VPC.
- Support for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integration) and explicit zero-copy of PHI to Redwood-hosted logs.
- On-prem installer or air-gapped bundle for isolated runs during certification windows.
- Network options: VPC peering or direct connect; strict egress control and allowlisting of minimal service endpoints.
- Model requirements: ability to pin a specific open model variant and freeze updates; fallback policy only on your approval.
- Expected volume: ~2M tokens/day with spikes up to 6M tokens/day during peak batch jobs. SLO ask: p95 latency under 200ms for typical inference paths; tolerant of longer for large-batch async jobs.

Blockers that will determine path forward
- Procurement: need a vendor attestation / SOC2 artifacts and NDA signed before detailed infra diagrams.
- KMS/HSM: confirmation that HSM provider integrates with our recommended connector (we support PKCS#11 and common cloud KMS APIs).
- Network: whether your security team can allow a small set of outbound IPs for control-plane telemetry, or if fully air-gapped install is required.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) I'll send our SOC2 summary + Redwood Private one-pager (attached).
2) CardioRisk to share redacted network diagram and a list of must-have egress restrictions (we'll treat that as a gating item).
3) We prepare an initial PoC scope (6-week, on-prem or in-VPC) and a rough pricing outline.
4) NDA / procurement: I'll drop the NDA link for signature — procurement timeline you mentioned is ~4–6 weeks.

Attachments referenced: [Redwood_Private_onepager.pdf], [SOC2_summary.pdf] — see attached.

If this matches your notes, I can loop in our infra SE (Monica) and schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/security lead next week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Private_onepager.pdf (PDF, 240KB)]
[Attachment: SOC2_summary.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Dr. Lana Ortiz <lana.ortiz@cardioriskhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel King <sam.king@cardioriskhealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery: private/on‑prem requirements — CardioRisk Health

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear write-up. This captures the main points. A few clarifications from our side:
- Procurement will need the SOC2 doc and a short vendor architecture before we can run the security review.
- For KMS we use a Thales HSM and expect your integration to support it; we can provide our PKCS#11 endpoint details after NDA.
- For the air-gap ask: we don't need daily air-gapped mode, but we must be able to perform a zero-network install and run cert-testing quarterly.

I'll pull together a redacted network diagram and send it over by Tuesday. Procurement also asked for an approximate cost band for a 6-week PoC and a 12-month committed tier — a ballpark is fine for now.

I'll sign the NDA once you share the DocuSign link.

Best,
Lana Ortiz
Chief of Clinical IT, CardioRisk Health
[Attachment: network_diagram_sketch.png (PNG, 85KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-08T19:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: CardioRisk next steps (POC scope + infra ask)

Marcus — quick internal note after the discovery call.

Key engineering questions to resolve before we draft POC SOW:
- HSM integration: confirm Thales model and whether they expose PKCS#11 + remote signing (Monica action: ask infra team).
- Air-gap installer: we should propose both an air-gapped linux bundle and a private-control-plane option. Need input from platform on estimated setup time (ETA: 2–3 weeks to prepare installer docs).
- Telemetry: propose minimal telemetry mode (heartbeat only) and an offline logs mode for their audit windows.

Pricing assumptions for ballpark to share with Marcus
- 6-week PoC: infra + SE time estimate — $45k–$65k depending on on-prem effort.
- 12-month committed: reserved capacity pricing; will prepare 2 options (standard + high-availability) for Neha to refine.

Attachments: initial POC scope draft (POC_scope_v1.md) for review.

I can take the lead on the technical deep-dive once Marcus confirms schedule and provides the redacted network diagram.

Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
